The '''2000–01 South African Premiership''', known as the 2000–01 '''Castle Premiership''' for sponsorship purposes, and also commonly referred to as the [[Premier Soccer League|PSL]] after the governing body, was the fifth season of the Premiership since its establishment in 1996. It was won by [[Orlando Pirates F.C.|Orlando Pirates]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lambley |first=Garrin |date=2023-08-03 |title=When last did Orlando Pirates win the DStv Premiership title? |url=https://www.thesouthafrican.com/sport/soccer/psl-south-africa/when-last-did-orlando-pirates-win-the-dstv-premiership-title-question-answer-result-faq-breaking-august-2023/ |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=The South African |language=en-ZA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Staff Reporter |date=2001-08-03 |title=Pirates seek more booty |url=https://mg.co.za/article/2001-08-03-pirates-seek-more-booty/ |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=The Mail & Guardian |language=en-ZA}}</ref>

[[Bloemfontein Celtic F.C.|Bloemfontein Celtic]] were fined R75,000 and deducted three points for fielding an ineligible player, and were relegated along with [[African Wanderers F.C.|African Wanderers]]. Both teams appealed their relegation, but were unsuccessful.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Staff Reporter |date=2001-06-01 |title=League season drags on |url=https://mg.co.za/article/2001-06-01-league-season-drags-on/ |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=The Mail & Guardian |language=en-ZA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Staff Reporter |date=2001-08-10 |title=PSL must stay on track |url=https://mg.co.za/article/2001-08-10-psl-must-stay-on-track/ |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=The Mail & Guardian |language=en-ZA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa 2000/01 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesz/zaf01.html |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=www.rsssf.org}}</ref>
